findings.title: Unknown outcomes are recorded as terminal and block all operator recovery
findings.issue: For model, speech and vision, the bare `except Exception` maps every non-`ModelProviderRejected` exception to `delivery_outcome='unknown'` and `retry_allowed=False`, including local pre-transport validation failures in message/payload construction (e.g. invalid bounded history or oversized request body) which never issued an HTTP request. In addition `execute_reserved`/`execute_reserved_groups` settle such failures as `outcome='unknown'`, which `settle()` treats as terminal (`state IN {'accepted','unknown'}`), so no later known actual can ever be applied and the logical task is permanently non
findings.fix: Distinguish local validation/authorization failures before transport from genuine transport indeterminacy and settle the former without marking the operation terminal, or add an explicit `awaiting_reconciliation` path that still accepts a later priced settlement.

not_verified: The claim that full test suite passes on this SHA.
Whether the model context/history reservation uses the same provider/connection scope as the text scope in all providers.
Whether delete_derived_in transitively cancels effect jobs awaiting reconciliation.
findings.summary: The two reported fixes (rejection vs invalid response classification and idempotent settle()) are present and appear correct, with one reservation state left terminal on unknown and a broader classification issue where pre-transport local validation failures collapse into `unknown`/non-retryable terminal state. No P0 defect found; the bounded media allowlists, revision monotonicity, migration fences and reader isolation show no concrete grant/permission escalation in this diff.
